fatal_errors: The proposed corrosion-only control cannot distinguish true wear-corrosion synergy from the unavoidable additional material loss caused by adding mechanical wear; wear-only and matched tribocorrosion controls are also required.

The hypothesis assumes preferential film formation and corrosion of a chemically active phase without evidence, whereas the target mechanism emphasizes temperature-dependent passive/tribo-layer repair and mechanical stability rather than phase-selective galvanic attack.
It omits the matched DS2205 comparator and therefore cannot recover the central alloy-to-alloy result.
It does not predict the observed non-monotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and maximum degradation at 100 °C.
It invokes an unspecified aggressive corrosive medium, while the relevant tribocorrosion tests used low-ionic-strength deionized water.
explanation: The response identifies a broadly plausible depassivation-repassivation feedback in which sliding ruptures an oxide and corrosion can facilitate further wear. This overlaps only with the high-temperature end of the target mechanism, where discontinuous oxide or tribo-layer patches repeatedly fracture and are removed. It misses the central temperature-dependent competition among abrasion, film repair, polishing, and third-body or oxidative wear, as well as the HEA's retained L12/B2 structure and DS2205's substantial phase redistribution. Conditions such as temperature, load, frequency, stroke, counter-body, exposure duration, thermal-shock history, and water chemistry are not reconstructed. The predicted outcome is generic synergy rather than the observed lower friction and roughly order-of-magnitude lower wear of the HEA, plus the 50 °C < 25 °C < 100 °C degradation ordering. The proposed microscopy and electrochemistry could test film rupture and localized corrosion, but the comparison cannot quantitatively separate wear, corrosion, and synergy. No supporting evidence is cited, so the phase-selective mechanism remains speculative.
